scientificAndSemanticReview.observation: Both languages retain the conflict between universally exact classical addition and invariant vacuum light speed. The codirectional train/light example yields Earth-frame c, explicitly not v+c.
The law is stated without proof for collinear motion only. Coincident X/X_1 and separately parallel Y/Y_1 and Z/Z_1 are all retained; Figure 226 is retained as a text reference only.
scientificAndSemanticReview.domainInterpretation: The special-relativity inertial-frame setting is inherited from the source context. The wording does not extend this one-dimensional scalar law to rotated axes or general three-dimensional motion.

scientificAndSemanticReview.observation: v remains K_1 relative to K; v_1 remains the object relative to K_1; v_2 remains the same object relative to K. Equation (8.6) is exactly v_2=(v_1+v)/(1+v_1v/c^2), with correct sign, c^2 and dimensions.
scientificAndSemanticReview.domainInterpretation: The source examples and speed-bound wording concern nonnegative speeds along the common motion direction. The same algebra permits signed collinear components, but the text does not advertise unsigned addition for arbitrary opposing directions.

scientificAndSemanticReview.observation: Both v<<c and v_1<<c are explicitly required. The correction v_1v/c^2 is dimensionless and neglected only in that regime. Chinese '近似' and English 'approximately' correctly qualify the retained classical equation.
The substitution v_1=c and full cancellation to v_2=c are unchanged and linked to the second postulate. For physical inertial-frame |v|<c, c+v is nonzero, so the cancellation is valid.
Both languages retain the light-speed bound and v_1=v=c giving 2c/2=c. '形式上的极限情形' and 'formal limiting case' correctly separate this source endpoint from physically realizable frame motion.
scientificAndSemanticReview.domainInterpretation: A material inertial frame has |v|<c; the equality v=c here is only the expressly formal limiting substitution. The independent inventory contains the codirectional inequality and signed-component identity supporting the bound, not an approval of a realizable light-speed frame.

scientificAndSemanticReview.observation: The rejection of v>c, earlier equation references (8.1)/(8.2) and imaginary calculated time/length are all retained. 'Physical meaning' accurately avoids representing imaginary values as physical readings.
scientificAndSemanticReview.domainInterpretation: v still denotes material frame motion in this lesson, not an unrelated phase or coordinate velocity.

scientificAndSemanticReview.observation: The maximum possible speed for transmitting interactions in nature is preserved in both languages. Light speed refers back to the vacuum c defined by the preceding source discussion.
